Task.title: Task
Task.description: Represents a single task within the DailyFlow application, including its details, status, and associated client.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Task entity.

title.description: The concise title or name of the task.

description.description: A detailed description of the task, potentially augmented by AI.

dueDate.description: The date and time by which the task is expected to be completed.

status.description: The current progress status of the task (e.g., 未着手, 進行中, 完了).

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the task was first created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the task was last updated.

clientId.description: Reference to the Client entity. (Relationship: Client 1:N Task)

Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client who will access specific tasks via a dedicated URL.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

name.description: The official name of the client.

dedicatedUrlIdentifier.description: A unique, client-friendly identifier used to generate a dedicated URL for task viewing. This should be unique across all clients.

contactEmail.description: The primary contact email address for the client.

description.description: Additional descriptive notes or internal information about the client.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the client record was first created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the client record was last updated.

definition.description: This collection serves as the Database Access Control (DBAC) for identifying administrative users. The existence of a document with a user's ID (`userId`) signifies that the user has administrative privileges. Used for enforcing admin-only access to /clients and /tasks.
Stores all client records, including their unique `dedicatedUrlIdentifier`. This collection is exclusively managed by administrative users.

params.name: clientId
params.description: The unique identifier of the client.

definition.description: Main storage for all task details, managed by administrative users. Each task document includes a `clientId` field linking it to a specific client.

params.name: taskId
params.description: The unique identifier of the task.

definition.description: A denormalized, read-only view of tasks specifically for client access via a dedicated URL. The `dedicatedUrlIdentifier` is denormalized into the path to ensure authorization independence and secure `list` operations without relying on `get()` calls in security rules. Task data from `/tasks/{taskId}` is copied here, with the `dedicatedUrlIdentifier` from the associated Client document.

params.name: dedicatedUrlIdentifier
params.description: The unique, client-friendly identifier used in the dedicated URL for accessing tasks.

params.name: taskId
params.description: The unique identifier of the task.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for DailyFlow prioritizes Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security Rules (QAPs) by employing both structural segregation and strategic denormalization. 

For **Admin Users** and internal management, we establish `/admin_users/{userId}` as a Database Access Control (DBAC) mechanism. The mere existence of a document in this collection grants administrative privileges to the corresponding `userId`. All core `Client` and `Task` data for administrative CRUD operations are stored in top-level collections: `/clients/{clientId}` and `/tasks/{taskId}`. Security rules for these collections will simply check for the `request.auth.uid`'s presence in `/admin_users`, ensuring atomic authorization checks without any `get()` calls to other documents.

For the **Client-Specific URL View** (取引先専用のURL), which requires read-only, potentially anonymous access to tasks linked to a specific client, Authorization Independence is achieved through **denormalization**. We introduce a dedicated path: `/client_task_views/{dedicatedUrlIdentifier}/tasks/{taskId}`. 

Here's how Authorization Independence and QAPs are satisfied:

1.  **Authorization Independence:** When an admin creates or updates a `Task`, the associated `Client`'s `dedicatedUrlIdentifier` is copied and becomes part of the path in this new collection. This means that a client trying to access `/client_task_views/{specificDedicatedUrlIdentifier}/tasks/{taskId}` will have the `dedicatedUrlIdentifier` directly available in the `path_param`. Security rules can then compare this `path_param` directly with the identifier presented in the client's request (e.g., from a URL segment or a custom token), completely eliminating the need for `get()` calls to a parent `Client` document or any other mapping collection. This ensures atomic authorization.

2.  **QAPs (Query-Aware Security Rules):** The structural segregation in `/client_task_views/{dedicatedUrlIdentifier}/tasks/{taskId}` inherently scopes queries. When a client performs a `list` operation on `/client_task_views/{specificDedicatedUrlIdentifier}/tasks`, the query is automatically limited to tasks associated with that `dedicatedUrlIdentifier`. The security rule only needs to verify that the requesting client's identifier matches the `path_param`, thus ensuring that rules are not acting as filters and only authorized data is retrieved. This also exemplifies **Structural Segregation**, where data with different security postures (admin R/W vs. anonymous R) are stored in distinct collections.

In summary, the design uses dedicated collections for admin roles, central collections for internal data management, and a denormalized, structurally segregated collection to provide secure, independent, and performant access for external clients. This approach minimizes security rule complexity and maximizes debuggability.
